**Date**: 2026-10-20 (inferred: Dudaško needs the register "by tomorrow" for the global meeting on Wed 2026-10-21)
**Attendees**: Kateřina Lesch (Dr. Max BDC, group AI; owner of the cross-country AI use-case register), Marek Pillár (BigHub, PM)
**Type**: external
**Recording**: N/A (Teams transcript, pasted)
**Previous session**: N/A (first meeting). Related: [2026-10-19 Finance (Deloitte + DUVo)](2026-10-19-finance-duvo-deloitte-analysis-global-ai-registry.md), where the global registry first came up.
**Meeting prep**: N/A

## TL;DR

Short first call with Kateřina Lesch, who owns the group's cross-country AI use-case register ("AI Use Case Register – Triage Edition"). Her goal is a **scoring methodology** that separates use cases too complex to integrate (they stay local) from good **group rollout candidates** (ROI + ease of implementation); reuse makes each further country rollout ~40% cheaper, and she wants to show leadership that CZ already has proven ones like MaxBuddy. Agreed: Marek fills the CZ rows **directly into her shared cloud register** (manual copy from his working file) and asks **Dudaško whether to fill the Impact/Scale/Feasibility scores**.

## Key Discussion Points

### 1. Lesch's goal: cross-group scoring and rollout

- **Kateřina Lesch** came straight from a cross-group use-case prioritisation meeting (with Jindřich). Each country keeps its own backlog, but the group needs a **scoring methodology** that shows (a) what is too complex to integrate and should stay in the country, and (b) which use cases are good rollout candidates on both ROI and implementation.
- She built the Excel register for all countries so they can be compared, and runs a **Claude artifact acting as a "portfolio manager"** on top of it that flags duplicates (e.g. "the Romanians and the Czechs are building exactly the same pharmacist assistant") `[translated from Czech]`.
- **Noise in submissions**: countries entered "every bit of nonsense", e.g. 6 HR use cases that are all the same RAG chatbot. These should come out of the scoring matrix as low value. The focus is what saves or generates the most money; "don't reinvent the wheel" `[translated from Czech]`.
- **Group vs. country incentives**: each country has its own incentives and KPIs, so it is hard for them to see that every further rollout is **~40% cheaper** when someone has already solved it. She wants MaxBuddy-type projects across the whole portfolio and to show leadership: "these four things are great, the Czechs have them done, connected to Farmis; Poland has some other animal, but it's worth doing" `[translated from Czech]`.

### 2. Who fills the benefit/score columns

- **Marek**: BigHub has mapped all its initiatives with an estimated benefit, but no delivery estimate or cost yet. Per the deal with Jindřich, he moves them into her global table (columns A–S). Open point: whether he, Dudaško, or Lesch fills the scoring columns, or whether that comes later.
- **Kateřina Lesch** acknowledged Marek can't know that yet. Marek will ask **Tomáš Dudaško** whether he fills them himself; Marek only knows the deadline from Jindřich, not how Dudaško presents it.

### 3. Future: demand-management tool

- **Kateřina Lesch**: the register will later move into a **demand-management tool** (in preparation) with scoring built in upfront. **Nothing should enter it without a quantified business value**: people "sucked ideas out of their thumbs", and some don't pay off, e.g. automating an accountant's work can cost more in tokens than the person does `[translated from Czech]`.

### 4. Where to fill it in

- The register sits **on Lesch's cloud** (shared). She asked Marek to fill it in there so she keeps the cross-country overview; Marek downloads a copy and copies the rows over manually ("good old-fashioned" manual work).
- **Marek** will add as much as possible: the **Deloitte/DUVo finance analysis** as one row, plus backlog items that aren't opened yet. He treats it as a high-management view for decision-making.

### 5. DUVo

- **Kateřina Lesch** runs her own **DUVo pilot in supply chain** with direct access to DUVo. In the finance analysis, by contrast, **Deloitte** enters Dr. Max's data into DUVo; Dr. Max doesn't work in DUVo directly. She seemed to think the DUVo finance work already has a business case calculated, then corrected herself towards Deloitte (unclear) — consistent with [[ASM-307]] (benefits TBD).

### 6. Roles and rapport

- Switched to informal "ty" at Lesch's suggestion; she finds the local culture very formal.
- She asked Marek's role (checking an unwanted agenda hadn't landed on him). **Marek**: product role, former product manager, agency background. Lesch: "That's what I need" `[translated from Czech]`.
- Possible lunch when Marek is at the Dr. Max office.
- **Kateřina Lesch**: glad CZ is this active. Other countries don't send the table at all (e.g. busy with acquisitions in Italy), while there is strong top-down pressure to deliver.

## Decisions Made

- **CZ rows go straight into Lesch's shared cloud register** (manual copy from Marek's working file), not sent separately.
- **Scores (Impact / Scale / Feasibility …)**: Marek doesn't fill them until Dudaško says who does.

Strategic signal: at group level CZ/BigHub work is seen as the model and a rollout source, which favours reusable, quantified use cases (MaxBuddy first) over country-specific ones.
